items.stem: Queries on a large events table cost more than expected. The table is partitioned by date. What most directly reduces bytes scanned?

options.text: Add a filter on the partitioning date column
options.rationale: Correct: a partition filter prunes partitions so fewer bytes are scanned.

options.text: Add SELECT * to return all columns
options.rationale: SELECT * scans more columns and raises cost.

options.text: Convert the query to a view without changing it
options.rationale: A view over the same query scans the same data.

items.explanation: Correct: a partition filter prunes partitions so fewer bytes are scanned.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO practices help control BigQuery query cost? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Select only the columns you need instead of all columns
options.rationale: Correct: fewer columns means fewer bytes scanned.

options.text: Filter on partitioned or clustered columns
options.rationale: Correct: pruning partitions and clusters reduces scanned data.

options.text: Always query the raw table with no filters
Duplicate the table before every query
options.rationale: Copying data adds storage cost and does not reduce query cost.

items.explanation: Correct: both keyed options are right; the distractors are wrong for the reasons given.

items.stem: A reporting team needs read access to a few columns of a sensitive table without seeing the rest. What is the best mechanism?

options.text: An authorized view exposing only the needed columns
options.rationale: Correct: authorized views grant scoped access without direct table access.

options.text: Grant Editor on the whole dataset
options.rationale: Editor exposes more than needed and allows changes.

options.text: Email a CSV export each morning
options.rationale: Manual exports are error-prone and not access control.
Public access exposes the sensitive data broadly.

items.explanation: Correct: authorized views grant scoped access without direct table access.
